Arctic terns can live for 30 years or more, and some birds like them migrate extremely long distances.
One tracked Arctic tern, traveling between the Arctic and Antarctica, flew about 96,000 kilometers in a single year.
Over a life of 30 years or more, a tern may fly the distance of several Moon round trips.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: Two fictional researchers studied how people judge distances while hiking.
Participants estimated the steepness of a hill.
Some participants wore a heavy backpack; others carried nothing.
Participants with heavy backpacks judged the hill to be steeper than participants without backpacks did.
The researchers concluded that people's sense of effort may influence how they perceive their surroundings.

stem: The student wants to present the study's conclusion. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: The goal is the conclusion, which B states. Distractors: A and D describe the method, and C gives the finding without the conclusion.
choices: In the study, some participants wore heavy backpacks and others carried nothing while estimating the steepness of a hill.
The researchers concluded that a person's sense of effort may shape how he or she perceives the surroundings.
Participants who wore heavy backpacks judged the hill to be steeper than participants who carried nothing did.
Two researchers studied how people judge distances while hiking.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: Sonia Sotomayor was born in the Bronx, New York, in 1954.
Her parents were from Puerto Rico.
She graduated from Princeton University and Yale Law School.
In 2009, she became a justice of the US Supreme Court.
She was the first Hispanic justice on the Supreme Court.

stem: The student wants to emphasize the historic nature of Sotomayor's appointment. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: C conveys the appointment's historic nature by noting she became the first Hispanic justice. Distractors: A and B give background; D gives the appointment without what made it historic.
choices: Sonia Sotomayor graduated from Princeton University and Yale Law School.
Sonia Sotomayor, whose parents were from Puerto Rico, was born in the Bronx in 1954.
When Sonia Sotomayor joined the US Supreme Court in 2009, she became its first Hispanic justice.
In 2009, Sonia Sotomayor became a justice of the US Supreme Court.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: The fictional ecologist Hana Kim studied two populations of the same lizard species.
One population lived on an island with many predators.
The other lived on an island with almost no predators.
Lizards on the predator-rich island had longer legs and ran faster.
Lizards on the predator-free island had shorter legs and spent more time in the open.

stem: The student wants to suggest a possible explanation for the difference between the two populations. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: The goal is an explanation for the difference. A connects the lizards' longer legs and faster speed to the presence of predators, offering a possible reason. Distractors: C and D describe the setup, and B gives one detail about one population, so none explains the difference.
choices: Longer legs and faster running may have helped lizards on the predator-rich island escape.
Lizards on the island with almost no predators had shorter legs.
Kim studied two populations of the same lizard species, one on an island with many predators and one on an island with almost none.
Kim's two islands differed: one had many predators, and the other had almost no predators at all.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: Kintsugi is a Japanese method of repairing broken pottery.
The cracks are filled with lacquer mixed with powdered gold, silver, or platinum.
The repairs are left visible rather than hidden.
The practice reflects the idea that an object's history, including damage, is part of its beauty.
Kintsugi may have begun in the late 1400s.

stem: The student wants to explain the philosophy behind kintsugi. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: The philosophy is the idea behind the practice. D states it and connects it to the visible repairs. Distractors: A gives its origin, B describes materials, and C describes the repairs without explaining why.
choices: Kintsugi, a Japanese method of repairing broken pottery with lacquer and powdered metal, may have begun in the late 1400s.
In kintsugi, a Japanese method of repairing broken pottery, cracks are filled with lacquer mixed with powdered gold, silver, or platinum.
Kintsugi repairs, made with lacquer mixed with powdered gold, silver, or platinum, are left visible rather than hidden.
Kintsugi leaves repairs visible because it treats an object's history, including damage, as part of its beauty.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: The fictional economist Peter Lindgren studied two neighboring towns.
Town A raised its minimum wage by 15 percent in 2018.
Town B kept its minimum wage the same.
Over the next three years, employment at restaurants grew 6 percent in Town A and 5 percent in Town B.
Lindgren cautioned that the towns differed in other ways, including tourism.

stem: The student wants to present Lindgren's findings while indicating that they don't prove the wage increase caused the employment change. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: A presents the findings and notes Lindgren's caution about other differences. Distractors: B describes only the policy; C gives the findings without the caution; D gives the caution without the findings.
choices: Restaurant jobs grew slightly faster in Town A, which raised its wage, but Lindgren noted the towns also differed in tourism.
Town A raised its minimum wage by 15 percent in 2018, while Town B did not.
Over the three years after 2018, restaurant employment grew 6 percent in Town A, which raised its minimum wage, and 5 percent in Town B.
Lindgren cautioned that the two towns differed in ways such as tourism.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: The novelist Toni Morrison was born in Lorain, Ohio, in 1931.
Her novel [i]Beloved[/i] (1987) won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.
In 1993, she won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
She was the first Black woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Before becoming a full-time writer, she worked as a book editor.

stem: The student wants to emphasize Morrison's achievements as a writer to an audience unfamiliar with her. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: For an unfamiliar audience, the sentence should identify Morrison and highlight her achievements. B does both. Distractors: A gives biography without achievements; C and D give a single achievement without identifying her as a novelist (D doesn't even name her).
choices: Toni Morrison, who was born in Lorain, Ohio, in 1931, worked as a book editor before becoming a full-time writer of novels such as [i]Beloved[/i].
Novelist Toni Morrison won a Pulitzer Prize for [i]Beloved[/i] and was the first Black woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
The Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to Toni Morrison in 1993.
[i]Beloved[/i] won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: Traditional maps of the world often use the Mercator projection.
The Mercator projection preserves the shapes of small areas, which makes it useful for navigation.
However, it greatly enlarges areas near the poles.
On a Mercator map, Greenland appears about as large as Africa.
In reality, Africa is about 14 times larger than Greenland.

stem: The student wants to illustrate a drawback of the Mercator projection with a specific example. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: C gives a specific example of distortion (Greenland and Africa) and shows the gap between appearance and reality. Distractors: A describes an advantage; B gives a fact without connecting it to the projection; D states the drawback without an example.
choices: The Mercator projection preserves the shapes of small areas, which makes it useful for navigation.
Africa is about 14 times larger than Greenland.
On a Mercator map, Greenland appears about as large as Africa, even though Africa is about 14 times larger.
The Mercator projection enlarges areas near the poles.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: The fictional archaeologist Diego Flores excavated a 1,000-year-old village in Peru.
He found the remains of large cooking pots in several houses.
The pots were big enough to cook for dozens of people.
He also found a large open plaza at the village's center.
Flores proposed that the villagers held communal feasts.

stem: The student wants to present the evidence for Flores's proposal. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: D presents both pieces of evidence and connects them to the proposal. Distractors: A states the proposal without evidence; B gives the setting and one piece of evidence without the proposal; C gives one piece of evidence without connecting it to the proposal.
choices: Flores, who excavated a 1,000-year-old village in Peru, proposed that the villagers who lived there held communal feasts.
Flores excavated a 1,000-year-old village in Peru and found the remains of cooking pots in several houses.
At the center of the 1,000-year-old Peruvian village that Flores excavated was a large open plaza.
Big cooking pots and a central plaza led Flores to propose that villagers held communal feasts.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: Light pollution is excess artificial light at night.
About 80 percent of the world's population lives under light-polluted skies.
Light pollution can disrupt the migration of birds, which use stars to navigate.
It can also confuse sea turtle hatchlings, which move toward the brightest horizon to find the ocean.
Shielded streetlights direct light downward and reduce light pollution.

stem: The student wants to emphasize that light pollution affects wildlife in more than one way. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: A shows two different effects on wildlife (birds and turtles). Distractors: B concerns people; C describes a solution; D gives only one effect.
choices: Light pollution can disrupt birds that navigate by the stars and confuse sea turtle hatchlings seeking the ocean.
About 80 percent of the world's population lives under light-polluted skies.
Shielded streetlights, which direct light downward, can reduce light pollution, the excess artificial light found at night.
Light pollution can confuse sea turtle hatchlings.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: The fictional musicologist Rachel Adeyemi studied recordings of a folk song collected in 1925 and 1965.
In 1925, the song was sung slowly and had eight verses.
In 1965, the song was usually sung faster and had only four verses.
Adeyemi found that by 1965, the song was often performed at dances.
She suggested that the song changed to suit its new use.

stem: The student wants to explain Adeyemi's interpretation of how and why the song changed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: The goal covers both how the song changed and why. C gives the changes (faster and shorter) and the reason (performances at dances). Distractors: A describes the study, B gives the changes without the reason, and D gives the new use without the change.
choices: Adeyemi studied recordings of a folk song collected in 1925 and in 1965, forty years apart, comparing the versions.
In 1925, the song was sung slowly and had eight verses; by 1965, it was usually sung faster and had only four.
Adeyemi suggested the song grew faster and shorter because it was increasingly performed at dances.
By 1965, the song was often performed at dances.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: Both the Arabic numeral system and the Roman numeral system are used to write numbers.
Arabic numerals use ten digits (0–9), and a digit's value depends on its position.
Roman numerals use letters such as I, V, X, L, C, D, and M.
Roman numerals have no symbol for zero.
Place value makes arithmetic with Arabic numerals much easier.

stem: The student wants to explain an advantage of Arabic numerals over Roman numerals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: D states an advantage (easier arithmetic) and its reason (place value). Distractors: A describes the symbols each system uses, B notes a similarity, and C states a fact about Roman numerals without explaining an advantage.
choices: Roman numerals use letters such as I, V, X, L, C, D, and M, while Arabic numerals use the ten digits 0 through 9.
Both the Arabic and Roman numeral systems are used to write numbers, though they use different symbols.
Roman numerals have no symbol for zero.
Thanks to place value, arithmetic is much easier with Arabic numerals than with Roman numerals.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: The fictional engineer Ayumi Sato designed a water filter made from sand, gravel, and charcoal.
It removes about 95 percent of bacteria from water.
It costs about $10 to build.
Commercial filters with similar performance cost about $60.
Sato hopes the filter can be used in villages without clean water.

stem: The student wants to emphasize why Sato's filter could be practical for villages without clean water. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: Practicality depends on effectiveness and cost. B shows the filter performs like commercial ones at a fraction of the cost. Distractors: A lists materials, C states her hope without reasons, and D concerns commercial filters only.
choices: Sato's filter is made from sand, gravel, and charcoal.
Sato's filter removes about 95 percent of bacteria, like commercial filters, but costs $10 instead of $60.
Sato, who designed a water filter made from sand, gravel, and charcoal, hopes it can be used in villages without clean water.
Commercial water filters can cost about $60.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: Octopuses have about 500 million neurons.
About two-thirds of those neurons are located in the octopus's eight arms rather than in its brain.
An octopus arm can react to touch and taste even after being separated from the body.
Some researchers describe octopus arms as having "a mind of their own."
Humans have about 86 billion neurons, most of them in the brain.

stem: The student wants to emphasize how the octopus's nervous system differs from a human's. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: The goal is a difference between the two nervous systems. B contrasts where most neurons are located in humans and octopuses. Distractors: A and C describe octopuses only; D compares the number of neurons but not how the systems are organized, and the notes emphasize organization, not count, as what makes octopuses unusual.
choices: Octopuses have about 500 million neurons, and some researchers say their arms have "a mind of their own."
Whereas most of a human's neurons are in the brain, about two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are located in its arms.
An octopus arm can react to touch and taste even after being separated from the body.
Humans have about 86 billion neurons, many more than octopuses have.

paras: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

items: The fictional sociologist Imani Brooks studied community gardens in four cities.
Gardeners reported eating more fresh vegetables after joining a garden.
Many gardeners said they had met neighbors they had not known before.
Brooks found that neighborhoods with gardens reported stronger feelings of trust among residents.
Brooks noted that people who join gardens may already be more social than others.

stem: The student wants to present one of Brooks's social findings and acknowledge a possible alternative explanation for it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
byHand: The goal has two parts: a social finding and an alternative explanation. D presents the finding about trust and Brooks's caution that gardeners may already be more social. Distractors: A gives a health finding; B gives a social finding without the alternative explanation; C gives the alternative explanation without a finding.
choices: Brooks found that gardeners ate more fresh vegetables after joining a community garden.
Many gardeners in Brooks's study of community gardens in four cities said they had met neighbors they hadn't known before joining.
Brooks noted that people who join community gardens may already be more social than people who do not join them.
Neighborhoods with gardens reported stronger trust, though gardeners may already be more social.

paras: Giraffes have very long necks, which let them reach leaves high in trees. ______ their necks contain only seven bones, the same number found in a human neck.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: It's unexpected that such a long neck has only seven bones, the same as a human's, so "Surprisingly" fits. Distractors: "Therefore" and "As a result" wrongly suggest the bone count is caused by the neck's length or its use; "Similarly" doesn't fit, since the second sentence isn't comparable to the first.

paras: The library extended its hours on weekends. ______ more students began using it to study on Saturdays and Sundays.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: More students studying on weekends is a consequence of the extended weekend hours, so "As a result" fits. Distractors: "However" and "In contrast" signal opposition; "For example" signals an illustration, not an effect.

paras: Penguins are birds, but they can't fly. ______ they are excellent swimmers, using their wings like flippers to move quickly through the water.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The second sentence describes what penguins do in place of flying, so "Instead" fits. Distractors: "For instance" would treat swimming as an example of not flying; "Similarly" signals likeness, and "Therefore" wrongly suggests that not flying causes excellent swimming.

paras: Many desert plants have special features that help them save water. ______ cacti store water in their thick stems and have spines instead of leaves, which reduces water loss.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Cacti are a specific case of desert plants with water-saving features, so "For example" fits. Distractors: "However" signals contrast; "In addition" and "Finally" add a new point rather than illustrating the first one.

paras: The first day of the science fair was rainy, so few people attended. ______ the second day was sunny, and the gym was crowded with visitors.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The second day differs from the first (sunny and crowded versus rainy and sparsely attended), so "By contrast" fits. Distractors: "Similarly" signals likeness; "For example" signals an illustration; "As a result" wrongly suggests the first day's weather caused the second day's crowds.

paras: To make bread, the baker first mixes flour, water, yeast, and salt. ______ she kneads the dough for about ten minutes and lets it rise.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The text describes steps in order, and kneading follows mixing, so "Next" fits. Distractors: "However" signals contrast, "In conclusion" signals a summary, and "For instance" signals an example.

paras: Exercise strengthens the heart and muscles. ______ it can improve mood and help people sleep better.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The second sentence adds more benefits of exercise, so "In addition" fits. Distractors: "Instead" and "In contrast" signal opposition; "For example" would make better mood and sleep examples of stronger hearts and muscles, which they aren't.

paras: The town's old bridge was too narrow for modern trucks. ______ the town built a new, wider bridge next to it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Building a wider bridge is a response to the old one being too narrow, so "Therefore" fits. Distractors: "However" signals contrast; "Similarly" signals likeness; "For instance" signals an example.

paras: Some people think that bats are blind. ______ most bats can see quite well, and many also use echolocation to find their way in the dark.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The second sentence corrects a mistaken belief, so "In fact" fits. Distractors: "Additionally" and "For example" would treat the second sentence as support for the first; "Consequently" signals a result.

paras: The novel was rejected by twelve publishers. ______ after it was finally published, it became a bestseller and was translated into thirty languages.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Becoming a bestseller contrasts with having been rejected twelve times, so "However" fits. Distractors: "Therefore" suggests the rejections caused its success; "Similarly" and "For example" don't signal the contrast.

paras: Elephants communicate in several ways. They trumpet loudly when excited or alarmed. ______ they make low rumbling sounds that can travel several kilometers through the ground.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The text lists ways elephants communicate, and rumbling is another way, so "They also" fits. Distractors: "Instead" suggests rumbling replaces trumpeting; "As a result" signals a consequence; "In conclusion" signals a summary.

paras: During the 1800s, many families traveled west across the United States in covered wagons. The journey could take five or six months. ______ the completion of the transcontinental railroad in 1869 made the same trip possible in about a week.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The railroad's completion came after the wagon era and changed travel times, so "Later" fits. Distractors: "For example" signals an illustration; "Similarly" and "In addition" don't convey the change over time.

paras: Maple trees produce sap that can be boiled down into syrup. It takes a lot of sap to make syrup. ______ about 40 liters of sap are needed to produce just 1 liter of maple syrup.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The third sentence gives a specific figure that emphasizes how much sap is needed, so "In fact" fits. Distractors: "However" and "Instead" signal contrast; "Meanwhile" signals events at the same time.

paras: The museum's main hall displays paintings from the 1600s. ______ the smaller rooms upstairs contain modern sculptures and photographs.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The text describes what's in two different parts of the museum at the same time, so "Meanwhile" fits. Distractors: "As a result" and "Therefore" signal cause and effect; "For example" would make the upstairs rooms an example of the main hall's paintings.

paras: Owls are able to turn their heads up to 270 degrees. This ability is important because owls can't move their eyes within their sockets. ______ turning their heads is the main way they look around.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Because owls can't move their eyes, turning their heads is how they look around, a conclusion that follows from the previous sentence, so "Thus" fits. Distractors: "In contrast" and "Nevertheless" signal contrast, and "For instance" signals an example.

paras: The city expected about 5,000 people to attend its first food festival. ______ more than 20,000 people came, and many vendors ran out of food by early afternoon.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The actual attendance differed sharply from what was expected, so "Instead" fits. Distractors: "For example," "Similarly," and "Additionally" don't signal the difference between expectation and outcome.

paras: Many people believe that goldfish have very short memories. Studies show that goldfish can remember things for months. ______ the popular belief about goldfish memory is wrong.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The final sentence draws a conclusion from the studies described before it, so "Therefore" fits. Distractors: "However" signals contrast; "For example" signals an illustration; "Meanwhile" signals events at the same time.

paras: Early critics dismissed the Impressionist painters, calling their loose brushstrokes sloppy and unfinished. ______ the movement's works now hang in major museums around the world and sell for millions of dollars.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The Impressionists' current prestige contrasts with their early dismissal, and the change happened over time, so "Today, however" fits. Distractors: "For this reason" suggests the dismissal caused their success; "Similarly" signals likeness; "In other words" signals a restatement.

paras: Researchers expected that students who studied with music playing would perform worse on memory tests. ______ students who listened to calm instrumental music performed just as well as those who studied in silence.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The result differed from what researchers expected, so "Contrary to that expectation" fits. Distractors: "As predicted" is the opposite; "For example" and "In addition" don't signal the contrast with the expectation.

paras: The Antarctic ice sheet contains about 90 percent of the world's ice. ______ if it melted completely, global sea levels would rise by about 58 meters.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Because the ice sheet holds so much of the world's ice, its melting would raise sea levels enormously; the second sentence is a consequence of the first, so "Consequently" fits. Distractors: "Nevertheless" and "In contrast" signal contrast; "For instance" signals an example.

paras: Some economists predicted that online shopping would put small bookstores out of business. For a time, many small stores did close. ______ in the past decade, the number of independent bookstores in the United States has grown.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The growth in bookstores contrasts with the earlier closures and happened later, so "More recently, however" fits. Distractors: "As a result" suggests the closures caused the growth; "For example" signals an illustration; "In other words" signals a restatement.

paras: The octopus has no bones, which allows it to change shape dramatically. ______ a large octopus can squeeze through an opening no bigger than a coin.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The second sentence gives a striking example that reinforces the claim about changing shape, so "Indeed" fits. Distractors: "However," "Instead," and "Nonetheless" signal contrast.

paras: The fictional historian Lena Ortiz argues that the printing press changed how ideas spread in Europe. Before the press, books were copied by hand and were rare and expensive. ______ printed books could be produced quickly and in large numbers, making them far more affordable.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Printed books are contrasted with hand-copied ones (quick and affordable versus rare and expensive), so "By contrast" fits. Distractors: "Similarly" signals likeness; "For instance" signals an example; "Thus" suggests the rarity of hand-copied books caused the speed of printing.

paras: Engineers designing the bridge had to account for strong winds, heavy traffic, and frequent earthquakes. ______ they used flexible steel joints that allow the structure to sway without breaking.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The flexible joints are the engineers' response to the challenges listed, so "To meet these challenges" fits. Distractors: "Despite these challenges" suggests the joints were used in spite of the challenges rather than because of them; "In addition to these challenges" would make the joints another challenge; "Like these challenges" makes no sense.

paras: Hummingbirds have the highest metabolism of any animal relative to their size. To fuel their rapid wingbeats, they must eat frequently. ______ a hummingbird may visit more than 1,000 flowers in a single day.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Visiting so many flowers is the result of needing to eat often, so "Accordingly" (consequently) fits. Distractors: "Nevertheless" and "In contrast" signal contrast; "Previously" signals an earlier time.

paras: The fictional composer Elena Vasquez wrote most of her early music for full orchestras. ______ her later works were written for just one or two instruments, a change she said reflected her growing interest in simplicity.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Her later works differ from her early ones, and the change happened over time, so "In her later career, however" fits. Distractors: "Likewise" signals likeness; "For example" signals an example; "As a result of this" suggests writing for orchestras caused the shift, which the text attributes to a growing interest in simplicity.

paras: Sea turtles return to the beaches where they hatched to lay their eggs, sometimes traveling thousands of kilometers. Scientists long wondered how they find their way. ______ studies suggest that the turtles may use Earth's magnetic field as a kind of map.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The studies are a newer development answering the long-standing question, so "Recently" fits. Distractors: "Nonetheless" signals contrast; "For instance" signals an example; "Similarly" signals likeness.

paras: Many people assume that the Sahara Desert has always been dry. ______ about 6,000 years ago, it was covered with grasslands, lakes, and rivers, and was home to hippos and crocodiles.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The second sentence corrects a common assumption, so "In reality" fits. Distractors: "Therefore" and "As a result" signal a consequence; "Similarly" signals likeness.

paras: Some companies have adopted four-day workweeks. Supporters argue that shorter weeks reduce burnout. ______ critics worry that customers will be frustrated if businesses are closed an extra day.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The critics' worry presents an opposing view to the supporters' argument, so "On the other hand" fits. Distractors: "For example," "Consequently," and "In other words" don't introduce an opposing view.

paras: The fictional chemist Ravi Patel spent years searching for a material that could store solar energy cheaply. His first several attempts failed. ______ his team developed a salt-based compound that stored heat for days at a low cost.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The successful compound came after years of failed attempts, so "Eventually" fits. Distractors: "Similarly" signals likeness; "For example" signals an illustration; "In contrast" signals a comparison between two things, not a later success.

paras: Earthworms may seem unimportant, but they play a major role in soil health. As they tunnel, they create spaces that let air and water reach plant roots. ______ their waste, called castings, adds nutrients to the soil.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The castings are a second way earthworms help soil, added to the tunneling, so "Moreover" fits. Distractors: "However" and "Instead" signal contrast; "For instance" would make castings an example of tunneling.

paras: The fictional poet Clara Weiss published only two books during her lifetime, and neither sold well. ______ after her death, a collection of her unpublished poems became one of the best-selling poetry books of the decade.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: It's an unexpected twist that her work became a bestseller only after her death, when it had sold poorly during her life, so "Ironically" fits. Distractors: "Therefore" suggests the poor sales caused the later success; "Likewise" signals similarity; "For example" signals an illustration.

paras: Polar bears are well suited to life in the Arctic. Their thick fur and a layer of fat keep them warm in freezing temperatures. ______ their large paws spread their weight, helping them walk on thin ice without breaking through.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Large paws are another adaptation to Arctic life, added to the fur and fat, so "Additionally" fits. Distractors: "In contrast" and "Nevertheless" signal contrast; "As a result" suggests fur and fat cause the large paws.

paras: When the fictional town of Millbrook built a new highway, officials expected it to reduce traffic on Main Street. ______ traffic on Main Street increased, because the highway brought more visitors to the town's shops.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Traffic increased rather than decreased, the opposite of what officials expected, so "Instead" fits. Distractors: "As expected" is the opposite; "For example" and "In addition" don't signal the reversal.

paras: The fictional linguist Amara Okafor argues that children don't learn grammar mainly by being corrected. Parents, she notes, rarely correct their children's grammar, focusing instead on whether what the children say is true. ______ children reliably master complex grammatical rules by the age of five.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Despite rarely being corrected, children still master grammar, so "Even so" signals the contrast between the lack of correction and the outcome. Distractors: "Therefore" suggests the lack of correction causes mastery; "Likewise" signals similarity; "That is" signals a restatement.

paras: Some scholars have argued that the ancient Maya abandoned their cities because of warfare. Others have pointed to overpopulation. ______ recent analyses of lake sediments suggest that a series of severe droughts may have played a major role.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The sediment analyses are a newer line of evidence suggesting another explanation, so "More recently" fits. Distractors: "For instance" would make drought an example of the earlier theories; "Consequently" signals a result; "In summary" signals a summary.

paras: The fictional biologist Hana Ito expected that frogs in polluted ponds would be smaller than frogs in clean ponds. Her measurements showed no difference in size. ______ frogs in the polluted ponds had far fewer offspring, suggesting that pollution affected them in ways that size alone could not reveal.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The final sentence reports a different effect of pollution after the first expectation wasn't confirmed, so "She did find, however, that" fits. Distractors: "For this reason" suggests the lack of size difference caused fewer offspring; "As she predicted" is wrong because she predicted a size difference; "In other words" signals a restatement.

paras: Coral reefs occupy less than one percent of the ocean floor. ______ they are home to about a quarter of all known marine species.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Supporting so many species contrasts with occupying so little space, so "Yet" fits. Distractors: "Accordingly" suggests a consequence; "Likewise" signals similarity; "For example" signals an illustration.

paras: Early telescopes produced blurry images with colored halos around stars. Isaac Newton concluded that the problem could not be solved with lenses alone, since lenses bend different colors of light by different amounts. ______ he designed a telescope that used a curved mirror instead of a lens to gather light.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Newton designed a mirror telescope because of his conclusion about lenses, so "With this in mind" fits. Distractors: "Nevertheless" and "In contrast" signal contrast; "Similarly" signals likeness.

paras: The fictional novelist Sofia Reyes is often praised for the realism of her dialogue. Her characters interrupt each other, trail off mid-sentence, and repeat themselves, much as people do in real conversation. ______ Reyes has said that she writes each line of dialogue many times, cutting and rearranging until it sounds unplanned.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: It's paradoxical that dialogue that sounds unplanned is the product of careful, repeated revision, so "Paradoxically" fits. Distractors: "Thus" suggests the realism causes her process; "Similarly" signals likeness; "For example" would treat her process as an example of characters interrupting each other.

paras: In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents had once been joined and had slowly drifted apart. Most geologists rejected the idea, partly because Wegener couldn't explain what force could move continents. ______ in the 1950s and 1960s, new evidence from the ocean floor revealed the process of seafloor spreading, and Wegener's idea gained wide acceptance.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The later acceptance contrasts with the earlier rejection and happened much later, so "Decades later, however" fits. Distractors: "As a result" suggests the rejection caused the acceptance; "For instance" signals an example; "In the same way" signals similarity.

paras: The fictional economist Marcus Lee found that people who received small, unexpected gifts were more likely to donate to charity afterward. He proposed that the gifts put people in a generous mood. ______ people who received gifts they had expected showed no increase in donations, suggesting that surprise, not the gift itself, was key.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The final sentence highlights an important additional finding that refines Lee's explanation, so "Notably" fits. Distractors: "Consequently" suggests the generous mood caused the result for expected gifts; "In other words" signals restatement; "Similarly" is wrong because expected gifts had a different effect.

paras: Most spiders spin a new web every day or two, eating the old silk to recycle its proteins. ______ some species maintain the same web for weeks, repairing small tears rather than starting over.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Spiders that keep the same web for weeks differ from most spiders, which spin new webs frequently, so "In contrast" fits. Distractors: "Therefore" signals a consequence; "For example" would make these species an example of frequent web-spinning; "Likewise" signals similarity.

paras: The fictional historian David Mensah argues that the textile mills of 1830s Massachusetts offered young women unusual independence. The women earned their own wages and lived away from their families. ______ Mensah acknowledges that the work was grueling, with shifts of twelve hours or more in noisy, crowded rooms.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Mensah acknowledges a downside alongside the independence he describes, so "At the same time" fits, introducing a contrasting consideration. Distractors: "For this reason" suggests independence caused the grueling work; "In other words" and "As an illustration" signal restatement or example.

paras: Plants can't move away from threats the way animals can. ______ many have evolved chemical defenses, producing toxins that make their leaves bitter or harmful to animals that eat them.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Chemical defenses make up for plants' inability to flee, so "To compensate" fits. Distractors: "In contrast" and "Nevertheless" signal contrast; "Similarly" signals likeness.

paras: The fictional astronomer Julia Park predicted that the comet would be visible to the naked eye in early March. ______ the comet broke apart as it neared the Sun, and by March it had faded to a dim smudge visible only through telescopes.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The comet's breakup disappointed those hoping to see it, and the outcome differed from the prediction, so "Unfortunately for observers" fits. Distractors: "As she predicted" contradicts the outcome; "For example" and "In addition" don't fit the reversal.

paras: Traditional economic models assume that people make decisions based on careful calculation. Behavioral economists, ______ have shown that people's choices are often shaped by habits, emotions, and how options are presented.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Behavioral economists' findings contrast with the traditional assumption of careful calculation, so "however" fits. Distractors: "For example" would make them an example of traditional models; "Therefore" signals a result; "Likewise" signals similarity.

paras: The fictional ecologist Sara Kim found that wolves in one national park hunted mostly at dawn and dusk. In a neighboring park where hikers were common during the day, ______ wolves hunted almost entirely at night, suggesting that they adjusted their behavior to avoid people.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: Wolves in the second park behaved differently from those in the first, so "by contrast" fits. Distractors: "For instance" signals an example; "As a result of this" suggests the first park's wolves caused the second park's behavior; "Similarly" signals likeness.

paras: Many scientists once thought that the deep ocean floor was nearly lifeless, since no sunlight reaches it. In 1977, however, researchers exploring hydrothermal vents found thriving communities of tube worms, clams, and crabs. ______ these animals depend not on sunlight but on bacteria that make food from chemicals in the vent water.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
byHand: The final sentence explains how life can exist without sunlight, revealing a discovered fact, so "As it turns out" fits. Distractors: "Nevertheless" signals contrast; "Similarly" signals likeness; "In conclusion" signals a summary.

paras: Every spring, thousands of toads in one English village cross a busy road to reach the pond where they breed. [u]For years, many of them were struck by cars.[/u] Then volunteers began carrying the toads across in buckets on rainy evenings, and the number killed each year dropped sharply.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The underlined sentence presents the danger the toads faced, and the next sentence describes how volunteers reduced it, so A is right. Distractors: It doesn't explain the breeding site (B), propose a road (C), or describe the volunteers' method (D), which comes afterward.
choices: It describes a problem that the volunteers' efforts later addressed.
It explains why the toads cross the road to breed in the pond.
It suggests that the village should build a new road away from the pond.
It describes how the volunteers carried the toads across the road in buckets.

paras: Most people think of honey as a simple sweet food. But honey has an unusual property: it almost never spoils. Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were thousands of years old and still safe to eat. Honey's low moisture and natural acidity make it very hard for bacteria to grow.

stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
byHand: The text states that honey almost never spoils (a surprising quality), gives the example of honey found in tombs, and then explains why (low moisture and acidity), so B is right. Distractors: It doesn't describe how honey is made (A), compare it with other foods (C), or present a debate (D).
choices: It describes how bees make honey and then explains how they store it in the hive.
It names a surprising trait of honey, gives an example, and explains its cause.
It compares honey with other foods and argues that honey is the healthier choice.
It presents a debate among archaeologists about ancient honey and then resolves it.

paras: The city of Seoul once had a highway running over a buried stream called Cheonggyecheon. In 2003, city leaders tore down the highway and uncovered the stream. Today, the area is a park where residents walk along the water, and summer temperatures there are several degrees cooler than on nearby streets.

stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
byHand: The text tells how Seoul removed a highway, uncovered a stream, and gained a cooler park, so C states its purpose. Distractors: It doesn't argue for all cities (A), explain the highway's construction (B), or compare traffic (D).
choices: To argue that all cities should remove their highways
To explain why Seoul built a highway over the stream
To describe how Seoul replaced a highway with a stream park and the benefits that followed
To compare traffic in Seoul before and after the highway was removed with traffic in other cities

paras: Chess players often memorize the first moves of many games, called openings. [u]Some grandmasters have studied thousands of these sequences.[/u] However, experts say that understanding why a move is good matters more than memorizing it, because opponents frequently play unexpected moves that take a game into unfamiliar territory.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The sentence illustrates the scale of memorization (thousands of sequences), setting up the "However" that follows, so B is right. Distractors: It doesn't explain opponents' moves (A); C contradicts the experts' view; D isn't what the sentence does.
choices: It explains why opponents often make unexpected moves.
It emphasizes how much effort some players put into memorizing openings.
It argues that memorizing openings is the most important chess skill.
It describes the rules for how a chess game begins.

paras: Many people believe that goldfish have a memory span of only a few seconds. Experiments tell a different story. Researchers have trained goldfish to push levers for food and found that the fish remembered the task months later.

stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
byHand: The text opens with the belief that goldfish forget within seconds, then reports experiments showing they remember for months, so D is right. Distractors: It doesn't list questions (A), give advice (B), or describe opposing experiments (C).
choices: It describes an experiment and then lists questions it raised.
It explains how goldfish are trained and then gives advice for pet owners.
It describes two experiments that reached opposite conclusions.
It presents a common belief and then gives evidence that contradicts it.

paras: The town of Riverside used to throw away tons of food scraps every week. In 2019, it began collecting the scraps separately and turning them into compost. [u]Local farmers now buy the compost to enrich their fields.[/u]

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The underlined sentence shows a positive result of the composting program (farmers buy the compost), so D is right. Distractors: It doesn't explain past waste (A), describe a problem (B), or blame farmers for the waste (C).
choices: It explains why the town once threw away food scraps.
It describes a problem with the town's compost program.
It suggests that farmers produced most of the town's food waste.
It shows one benefit of the town's composting program.

paras: In 1928, scientist Alexander Fleming returned from vacation to find mold growing in one of his dishes of bacteria. He noticed that the bacteria near the mold had died. Curious, he studied the mold and discovered that it produced a substance that killed bacteria. That substance, penicillin, became one of the first antibiotics.

stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
byHand: The text tells how Fleming noticed mold killing bacteria by chance and went on to discover penicillin, so A states its purpose. Distractors: B misreads a detail; C and D make claims the text doesn't make.
choices: To recount how an accidental observation led to an important discovery
To explain why scientists should take vacations
To describe the different kinds of mold that grow in laboratories
To argue that penicillin is the best antibiotic available today

paras: Some birds use tools. [u]New Caledonian crows, for example, bend twigs into hooks to pull insects out of holes in trees.[/u] Scientists once believed that only humans and a few other primates could make tools, but birds like these have challenged that idea.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The underlined sentence follows the claim that some birds use tools and offers a specific case, so B is right. Distractors: It isn't about nests (A) or why scientists study primates (C), and it makes no comparison of intelligence (D).
choices: It describes where New Caledonian crows build their nests.
It gives a specific example of a bird using a tool.
It explains why scientists study primates.
It argues that crows are smarter than primates.

paras: Every year, a small library in rural Maine lends out more than books. Patrons can borrow fishing rods, snowshoes, telescopes, and even cake pans. The library's director says the goal is to give residents access to things they might use only a few times a year and not want to buy.

stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
byHand: The text says the library lends more than books, lists examples (fishing rods, snowshoes, and so on), and gives the director's explanation, so C is right. Distractors: It doesn't present a problem (A), compare libraries (B), or discuss books (D).
choices: It describes a problem that a library faces and then proposes a solution.
It compares a rural library with libraries in large cities.
It introduces an unusual library practice, gives examples, and explains its purpose.
It lists the most popular books at a library and explains why residents enjoy them.

paras: Many people assume that the color of an egg's shell says something about its nutrition. In fact, shell color depends mainly on the breed of the hen that laid it. A brown egg and a white egg from hens raised on the same diet are nutritionally almost identical.

stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
byHand: The text states a common assumption and then explains that shell color reflects breed, not nutrition, so D is right. Distractors: It makes no recommendation (A), doesn't explain how hens are raised (B), and doesn't discuss change over time (C).
choices: To recommend that people buy brown eggs instead of white eggs
To explain how hens of different breeds are raised
To describe how the color of eggshells has changed over time
To correct a common belief about eggshell color

paras: Glass frogs, found in Central and South American rainforests, have skin on their bellies that is almost completely transparent. [u]Looking at a glass frog from below, an observer can see its heart beating.[/u] Researchers think the see-through skin may help the frogs blend in with the leaves where they rest during the day.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The underlined sentence shows just how see-through the skin is (one can see the heart beating), so A is right. Distractors: It doesn't concern food (C), extinction (B), or disagreement with the researchers (D).
choices: It illustrates how transparent the frogs' skin is.
It suggests that glass frogs are in danger of extinction.
It explains how glass frogs find food.
It challenges the researchers' explanation of the frogs' skin.

paras: Before refrigerators were common, many households used iceboxes. Every few days, an "iceman" delivered a large block of ice, which was placed in a compartment at the top of the box. As the ice slowly melted, it kept food in the compartments below cool.

stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
byHand: The text explains how iceboxes and ice deliveries kept food cool before refrigerators, so A states its purpose. Distractors: It makes no comparison of effectiveness (B), says nothing about harvesting ice (C), and mentions the iceman only as part of how iceboxes worked (D).
choices: To describe how food was kept cold before refrigerators
To argue that iceboxes worked better than the modern refrigerators that replaced them
To explain how ice was harvested from frozen lakes each winter and stored
To describe the daily life of the people who delivered ice

paras: Some people say that you can't teach an old dog new tricks. [u]Researchers at a university in Vienna decided to test this saying.[/u] They found that older dogs did learn new tasks, though more slowly than younger dogs, and that they remembered what they learned just as well.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The underlined sentence moves from the saying to the research that tested it, introducing the study whose results follow, so D is right. Distractors: It doesn't explain slower learning (A), give results (C), or argue that the saying is true (B).
choices: It explains why older dogs learn more slowly than younger dogs.
It argues that the common saying is accurate.
It describes the results of a study on dogs' memories.
It introduces a study that examined a common saying.

paras: Many historians have portrayed the Erie Canal, completed in 1825, as an engineering triumph that transformed New York's economy. Historian Carol Sheriff accepts this view but adds a complication. [u]She shows that the canal also brought unwelcome changes to many towns along its route, including crowded docks, rising land prices, and conflicts over who should pay for repairs.[/u] For many residents, Sheriff argues, progress was a mixed blessing.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: Sheriff "accepts this view but adds a complication"; the underlined sentence lists the unwelcome changes that make up that complication, so B is right. Distractors: A contradicts her acceptance of the common view; C and D describe things the sentence doesn't address.
choices: It challenges the claim that the canal was an engineering achievement.
It gives evidence of the complication Sheriff adds to the usual view.
It explains why the canal was completed in 1825 rather than earlier.
It describes the economic benefits that the canal brought to New York.

paras: Bioluminescence, the production of light by living things, is rare on land but common in the deep ocean, where sunlight doesn't reach. Some deep-sea fish use glowing lures to attract prey. Others flash light to startle predators. Still others, such as certain shrimp, release clouds of glowing fluid, like a squid releasing ink, to escape. In the darkness of the deep sea, light has become a tool for survival in many different ways.

stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
byHand: The text introduces bioluminescence, gives examples (lures, flashes, glowing clouds), and concludes that light is a survival tool in many ways, so C is right. Distractors: A misdescribes the examples as solutions to a problem; B is wrong because the text never explains the chemistry; D overstates a single brief comparison.
choices: It describes a problem facing deep-sea animals and then proposes several solutions.
It explains how bioluminescence works chemically and then describes where it is found.
It introduces a phenomenon, gives several examples of how animals use it, and then states a general conclusion.
It compares bioluminescence on land with bioluminescence in the ocean and argues that one is more useful.

passage.text: The following text is adapted from a 1912 short story.

paras: The house at the end of Linden Street had been empty for so long that the children of the neighborhood had invented a dozen histories for it. [u]Some said a sea captain had died there; others insisted it was haunted by a woman in a gray dress.[/u] When at last a moving truck pulled up one summer morning, every child on the street found a reason to walk past.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The previous sentence says the children "invented a dozen histories" for the house; the underlined sentence gives two of them, so D is right. Distractors: A is wrong because the stories are invented; B isn't addressed; C is contradicted by the children's eagerness to walk past.
choices: It reveals the true history of the house that stood at the end of Linden Street.
It explains why the new family chose to move into the empty house.
It suggests that the children were afraid to walk past the house.
It gives examples of the histories the children had invented.

paras: Researchers have long known that sleep helps people remember what they have learned, but the reason has been unclear. Neuroscientist Jamal Reid's team recorded brain activity in volunteers who learned a sequence of finger movements before napping. During the nap, the same brain regions that had been active during learning became active again, in the same order. [u]Volunteers whose brains showed the most replay improved the most when they practiced the task after waking.[/u]

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The text describes brain regions replaying during sleep; the underlined sentence connects the amount of replay to improvement after waking, which supports replay as the reason sleep helps memory. D is right. Distractors: The sentence doesn't describe a limitation (A), explain the choice of task (B), or suggest the nap was too short (C).
choices: It describes a limitation of Reid's study.
It explains why the volunteers learned a sequence of finger movements.
It suggests that the volunteers did not sleep long enough to benefit from the nap.
It presents a finding that links the brain replay during sleep with improved performance.

paras: Economists usually assume that people make decisions by weighing costs and benefits. But behavioral economist Ruth Feldman points out that many people who sign up for gym memberships rarely use them, paying for months of visits they never make. Feldman argues that people often overestimate how disciplined their future selves will be, a pattern that standard economic models struggle to explain.

stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
byHand: The text states the usual assumption, offers the gym example that doesn't fit it, and gives Feldman's explanation, so A states its purpose. Distractors: B and D aren't the text's focus; C misreads the opening sentence, which states an assumption rather than describing a method.
choices: To present an example that challenges a standard assumption and an explanation for it
To argue that gym memberships should cost less, since many members rarely use the gym at all
To describe how economists calculate the costs and benefits of decisions
To explain why exercise is beneficial for people's health

paras: When the city of Linton planned a new light-rail line, officials expected most riders to be commuters. Surveys after the line opened showed something different. [u]More than half of riders were traveling for errands, shopping, or social visits rather than for work.[/u] Planners have since used the findings to adjust train schedules, adding more service on weekends and in the evenings.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The previous sentence says the surveys showed "something different"; the underlined sentence specifies what (most riders weren't commuting), so A is right. Distractors: B, C, and D describe things the sentence doesn't do.
choices: It specifies the survey finding that differed from officials' expectations.
It explains why city officials expected most riders of the new line to be commuters.
It describes a problem with the way the surveys were conducted.
It argues that the light-rail line should not have been built.

paras: The violin makers of Cremona, Italy, including Antonio Stradivari, produced instruments in the 1600s and 1700s that are still prized for their sound. Many theories have tried to explain their quality: special varnishes, chemical treatments of the wood, or even unusually cold weather that produced denser trees. Yet in blind tests, some professional violinists have been unable to tell the old instruments from the best modern ones, and many have preferred the modern ones.

stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
byHand: The text introduces the Cremona violins, lists several theories for their quality, and then describes blind tests that question whether the old violins are really superior, so D is right. Distractors: A misdescribes the text, which doesn't explain how violins are made; B is wrong because the text lists several theories; C is wrong because it isn't a biography.
choices: It describes how violins are made and then explains why modern violins are better.
It presents a single theory about the Cremona violins' quality and then supports it with evidence from blind tests.
It recounts the life of Antonio Stradivari and then describes his influence on later violin makers in Cremona and beyond.
It introduces prized violins, lists theories for their quality, and then questions the assumption behind those theories.

paras: Coffee plants produce caffeine, which is toxic to many insects in high doses. Yet scientists have found that coffee flowers contain small amounts of caffeine in their nectar. [u]Rather than driving pollinators away, these low doses seem to improve bees' memory of the flowers' scent, making the bees more likely to return.[/u]

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The text sets up a puzzle (caffeine is toxic to insects, yet it appears in nectar), and the underlined sentence resolves it with a surprising benefit: improved memory in bees. A is right. Distractors: B describes the earlier point about toxicity; C overstates; D isn't discussed.
choices: It explains a surprising effect of the caffeine found in coffee nectar.
It describes how caffeine in high doses harms insects that eat coffee leaves.
It argues that bees prefer coffee flowers to all other flowers they visit.
It describes how scientists measured caffeine levels in nectar.

paras: In 1977, Wangari Maathai founded the Green Belt Movement in Kenya, encouraging rural women to plant trees. The trees provided firewood and fruit and helped prevent soil erosion. But the movement did more than plant trees: by organizing women into groups, it gave them experience in leadership and a stronger voice in their communities. Maathai later became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
byHand: The text describes the Green Belt Movement and its effects, both environmental (firewood, fruit, soil) and social (leadership and a stronger voice for women), so C states its purpose. Distractors: A and B take up details the text doesn't develop; D makes a comparison the text never makes.
choices: To explain the causes of soil erosion in Kenya
To describe the process of planting and caring for trees
To describe a movement and its environmental and social effects
To compare the Green Belt Movement with other environmental groups

paras: Many people picture the Sahara as an endless sea of sand dunes. [u]In fact, dunes cover only about a quarter of the desert.[/u] Much of the rest consists of rocky plateaus, gravel plains, and mountains, some of which receive snow in winter.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The first sentence gives a common image; the underlined sentence ("In fact...") starts to correct it, and the last sentence continues the correction. C is right. Distractors: A isn't discussed; B is the opposite; D describes the following sentence.
choices: It explains how sand dunes form in the desert.
It supports the common image of the Sahara described in the first sentence.
It begins to correct a common misconception about the Sahara.
It describes the mountains of the Sahara.

paras: Historians often describe the invention of the printing press as a sudden revolution. But printed books did not replace handwritten ones overnight. For decades after Gutenberg's press appeared in the 1450s, scribes continued to copy texts by hand, and some wealthy readers preferred handwritten books, which they saw as more elegant. Printing transformed European culture, but it did so gradually.

stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
byHand: The text presents the "sudden revolution" view, offers evidence that the change was slower, and concludes that printing transformed culture "gradually," so B is right. Distractors: A misdescribes the text, which doesn't explain how the press worked; C confuses some readers' preference with the author's argument; D isn't what the text does.
choices: It describes Gutenberg's invention in the 1450s and then explains how the printing press worked.
It presents a common view, qualifies it with details, and restates it in a more balanced form.
It compares printed books with handwritten ones and argues that wealthy readers were right to prefer handwritten books.
It lists several inventions of the 1450s and ranks them by importance.

paras: The Japanese art of kintsugi repairs broken pottery with lacquer mixed with powdered gold. [u]Rather than hiding the cracks, the gold makes them shine.[/u] Practitioners see the repaired object as more beautiful for having been broken, a philosophy that treats damage as part of an object's history rather than something to disguise.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The underlined sentence contrasts kintsugi with hiding cracks, preparing for the philosophy that damage is part of an object's history. B is right. Distractors: The sentence doesn't explain the mixing process (A), claim gold is strongest (C), or give a history (D).
choices: It explains how the lacquer and powdered gold used in kintsugi are mixed together.
It contrasts kintsugi with repairs that try to hide damage.
It argues that gold is the strongest material for repairing pottery.
It describes the history of kintsugi and how it spread in Japan.

paras: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all known marine species. Scientists sometimes call them "rainforests of the sea." Reefs also protect coastlines from storms and provide food and income for hundreds of millions of people. Rising ocean temperatures, however, now threaten many reefs worldwide.

stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
byHand: Most of the text describes why reefs matter (species, coastline protection, food and income), and the last sentence names a threat, so A is right. Distractors: B isn't discussed; C overstates a single nickname; D is wrong because no solutions are proposed.
choices: To explain the importance of coral reefs and note a threat they face
To describe how coral reefs form over time
To compare coral reefs with rainforests on land
To propose ways to protect coral reefs from rising temperatures

paras: Anthropologists studying hunter-gatherer groups have often emphasized how much time people spend searching for food. Anthropologist Ama Boateng's research with one group in the Kalahari offers a different picture. [u]She found that adults spent, on average, fewer than twenty hours a week on activities related to finding and preparing food, and devoted much of the remaining time to storytelling, music, and visiting relatives.[/u] Boateng cautions, however, that her findings come from a single year with unusually plentiful rainfall.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The text says Boateng "offers a different picture"; the underlined sentence gives the specific findings that make up that picture. B is right. Distractors: A misreads the sentence's focus; C describes the final sentence; D overgeneralizes. Boateng studied one group and notes a limitation.
choices: It explains why earlier anthropologists emphasized time spent searching for food.
It presents the findings behind Boateng's different picture of hunter-gatherer life.
It describes the limitation that Boateng acknowledges in her research.
It argues that all hunter-gatherer groups spend little time searching for food.

paras: For centuries, scholars assumed that the Inca, who left no known written texts, had no system for recording information. That assumption has been challenged by the study of khipu, bundles of knotted strings. Researchers have shown that many khipu recorded numbers, such as census figures and tax records, using knots in different positions. Some scholars now argue that certain khipu may also have recorded words or narratives, though no one has yet deciphered them.

stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
byHand: The text gives the assumption that the Inca had no recording system, presents evidence that khipu recorded numbers, and ends with the unconfirmed idea that some may record words. C is right. Distractors: A and B misdescribe the text, which doesn't explain how khipu were made, compare them with written texts, or argue for one theory; D contradicts the statement that no one has deciphered the possible word-recording khipu.
choices: It describes how khipu were made from knotted strings and then compares them with written texts from other cultures.
It presents two competing theories about khipu and argues that one is correct.
It describes a long-held assumption, offers evidence against it, and notes an unconfirmed possibility.
It explains how researchers deciphered the khipu and then describes what the words and numbers on them say.

passage.text: The following text is adapted from a novel. Ilse, a young singer, is listening to a concert.

paras: Ilse had heard the symphony described as melancholy, and she had come prepared to be sad. But as the music went on, she felt instead a kind of fierce happiness, as if someone had opened a window in a room she had not known was stuffy. [u]She did not know whether the critics had been wrong or whether she had simply heard a different symphony from the one they had heard.[/u]

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: Ilse expected sadness but felt "fierce happiness"; the underlined sentence shows her wondering about the difference between the critics' view and her own response. C is right. Distractors: A contradicts her experience; B is wrong because the sentence doesn't explain the critics' view; D isn't suggested.
choices: It reveals that Ilse has come to agree with the critics' description of the symphony as melancholy.
It explains why the critics described the symphony as melancholy.
It shows Ilse weighing others' descriptions of the music against her own experience of it.
It suggests that Ilse plans to become a music critic.

paras: It is tempting to conclude that the ancient city of Cahokia, near present-day St. Louis, was abandoned because its residents exhausted local forests and caused severe flooding. Archaeologist Caitlin Rankin tested this idea by examining soil layers near the city's mounds. She found no evidence of the erosion and flood deposits that widespread deforestation would have produced. [u]Rankin's findings do not explain why Cahokia's population declined, but they make one popular explanation less likely.[/u]

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The underlined sentence notes what Rankin's findings don't do (explain the decline) and what they do (make one explanation less likely), so it clarifies their limits and significance (A). Distractors: B is wrong because it offers no new explanation; C describes the earlier sentence; D overstates. The findings argue against widespread deforestation, not any tree cutting.
choices: It clarifies the limits and significance of Rankin's findings.
It presents a new explanation for why Cahokia was abandoned.
It describes the method Rankin used to examine the soil.
It argues that the city's residents did not cut down any trees.

paras: Many studies have found that people who own dogs tend to be more physically active than people who don't. Some have concluded that owning a dog causes people to exercise more. Epidemiologist Tove Lind points out a problem with that conclusion: people who already enjoy exercise may be more likely to get dogs in the first place. To address this, Lind's team compared the same people's activity levels before and after they acquired dogs.

stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
byHand: The text presents a conclusion (dogs cause exercise), identifies an alternative explanation (active people get dogs), and describes a study designed to test it, so D is right. Distractors: The other choices take up details or claims the text doesn't develop.
choices: To argue that dog owners are healthier and more active than people who own other pets
To describe the health benefits of walking a dog every day for people of all ages
To explain why people who already enjoy exercise are more likely to choose to get dogs
To describe a possible flaw in a conclusion and a study designed to test it

paras: Some critics have described the fictional poet Rosa Ibarra's early work as simple, even naive, pointing to its short lines and plain vocabulary. [u]Yet those same features allowed Ibarra to pack her poems with double meanings: a single plain word, placed at the end of a short line, often reads one way on its own and another way when the next line begins.[/u] What looks like simplicity, in other words, is often a deliberate kind of compression.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The critics see short lines and plain words as naive; the underlined sentence ("Yet...") argues those same features create double meanings, offering a different interpretation. B is right. Distractors: A reverses the sentence's role; C and D introduce topics the text never addresses.
choices: It provides an example of the naive quality that the critics identify in Ibarra's early work.
It presents a different interpretation of the features that the critics point to.
It explains why Ibarra later abandoned short lines and plain vocabulary.
It describes the influence of other poets on Ibarra's early work.

paras: The planet Venus rotates so slowly that a single day there lasts longer than its year. Stranger still, it rotates in the opposite direction from most planets, so the Sun rises in the west. Scientists have proposed several explanations: a collision with a large object early in Venus's history, or the gradual effect of tides in its thick atmosphere. Neither explanation has been confirmed, and Venus's unusual spin remains an open question.

stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
byHand: The text describes Venus's slow, reversed rotation, offers two possible explanations, and states that neither is confirmed. B is right. Distractors: A focuses on temperature, which the text doesn't discuss; C makes a comparison the text doesn't make; D contradicts "Neither explanation has been confirmed.".
choices: It describes Venus's thick atmosphere and then explains how that atmosphere affects the planet's temperature.
It describes Venus's unusual rotation, offers possible explanations, and notes the question is unresolved.
It compares Venus with Earth and argues that the two planets formed in the same way.
It presents a theory about Venus's rotation and then gives evidence from tides and collisions that confirms it.

paras: In the 1850s, many London doctors believed that cholera spread through "bad air." Physician John Snow suspected contaminated water instead. [u]When an outbreak struck the Soho neighborhood in 1854, he marked each death on a map and found that the deaths clustered around a single public water pump on Broad Street.[/u] After the pump's handle was removed, new cases in the area declined, though historians note that the outbreak was already fading by then.

stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
byHand: The text gives Snow's suspicion that water spread cholera; the underlined sentence describes how he gathered evidence, mapping deaths that clustered around one pump. C is right. Distractors: A describes the opposing theory, B describes the last sentence's qualification, and D overstates. The final sentence adds a note of caution.
choices: It describes the "bad air" theory that most London doctors believed.
